markdown.markdown:
Five scoreboard products, all built from the same 20 Hz player tracking:
**Burner Board**, **Home-to-First Dash**, **Fastest Out of the Box**,
**Extra-Base Instinct**, and **Pickoff Jump**.


Speed is finite-differenced from consecutive tracking frames. A single mistracked
frame can produce an absurd instantaneous value, so peak speed is taken as a
**high percentile rather than the maximum** — a runner who does it repeatedly
outranks one lucky frame.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-speed-core
#| eval: false
frame_speed <- function(x, y, timestamp) {
  dt <- diff(timestamp) / 1000
  d  <- sqrt(diff(x)^2 + diff(y)^2)
  ifelse(dt > 0, d / dt, NA_real_)
}

top_speed <- function(x, probs = 0.90) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  unname(stats::quantile(x, probs = probs, na.rm = TRUE))
}
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-speed-core
#| eval: false
def top_speed(speeds, pct=90):
    s = np.asarray(speeds, dtype=float)
    s = s[np.isfinite(s)]
    if s.size == 0:
        return np.nan
    return float(np.percentile(s, pct))
```

:::

## Burner Board

Peak sprint speed on the way to first, ranked across the league.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-burner
#| eval: false
source("../R/R04_speed_baserunning.R")

board <- burner_board(sprints, lineups, min_runs = 3, top = 10)
board
plot_burner_board(board)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-burner
#| eval: false
from components import c03_tracking_features as c03, c04_speed_baserunning as c04
from smtstory import dataio

tabs = c03.load_feature_tables()
lu = dataio.load_lineups()
c04.burner_board(tabs["sprints"], lu, top=10)
```

:::

| player | top speed (mph) | avg (mph) | runs | percentile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VAS-1487 | **22.76** | 16.91 | 114 | 100.0 |
| OSW-0976 | 22.05 | 16.38 | 11 | 99.9 |
| AVV-6439 | 22.01 | 18.81 | 6 | 99.8 |
| VAS-5976 | 21.99 | 17.26 | 100 | 99.6 |

![Burner Board](../outputs/figures/fig_burner_board.png)

::: {.callout-note}
League context: sprint speed averages 16.3 mph with a 90th percentile of
19.6 mph across 11,726 tracked runs, so 22.8 mph is genuinely exceptional.
:::

## Home-to-First Dash

Elapsed time from contact to the first-base bag — measured as the moment the
runner enters a 4-foot radius of the bag, not estimated from speed.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-h2f
#| eval: false
home_to_first(runs_tbl, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-h2f
#| eval: false
c04.home_to_first(anatomy_rows, top=10)
```

:::

Times are graded ELITE (< 4.2 s), PLUS (< 4.5 s) or AVERAGE — the same
thresholds a scout uses, which is what makes the graphic legible.

## Fastest Out of the Box

Acceleration in the first 1.5 seconds, which is the window in which reaction and
first step actually show up.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-burst
#| eval: false
compute_burst <- function(track, t_hit, window_ms = 1500) {
  w  <- dplyr::filter(track, timestamp >= t_hit, timestamp <= t_hit + window_ms)
  sp <- frame_speed(w$field_x, w$field_y, w$timestamp)
  sp <- sp[is.finite(sp)]
  (max(sp) - sp[1]) / (window_ms / 1000)
}
out_of_the_box(runs_tbl, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-burst
#| eval: false
c04.out_of_the_box(anatomy_rows, top=10)
```

:::

## Extra-Base Instinct

Top speed and path efficiency when a runner actually takes an extra base —
filtered to plays the reconstruction scored as a double or triple.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-extra
#| eval: false
extra_base_instinct(pbp, sprints, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-extra
#| eval: false
c04.extra_base_instinct(pbp, tabs["sprints"], lu, top=10)
```

:::

Path efficiency is straight-line distance ÷ actual distance travelled: 1.0 is a
perfect line, and anything below about 0.9 on the bases is a wide turn.

## Pickoff Jump

::: {.callout-warning}
## Scope: measured, not modelled

The data flags pickoff attempts (`is_pickoff`) but records **no outcome**, and
there are no stolen-base or caught-stealing labels anywhere in the dataset. A
"steal success probability" would therefore be invented, not learned.

This product reports what the tracking actually shows: the runner's **secondary
lead distance** off the bag at the moment of the pitch, and his **burst**. Both
are real measurements a fan can see confirmed on the replay.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

### R

```{r}
#| label: r-pickoff
#| eval: false
pickoff_jump("y1_d122_IOL_VAS", lineups, top = 10)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: py-pickoff
#| eval: false
c04.pickoff_jump(game, lu, top=10)
```

:::
